ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an upper nitrogen-containing six-membered heteroaromatic ring, with a CF3 substituent connected at the upper right; this upper ring is connected to the lower benzene ring through an oxygen atom; the lower benzene ring is then connected to a side chain containing C=C, and the end of the side chain is connected to two methoxy/alkoxy fragments. There are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows, and excluding all bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning count: Count by structural blocks, and each heavy-atom bond is counted only once. The upper nitrogen-containing heteroaromatic ring has 6 intra-ring bonds; the CF3 substituent has 1 ring-C bond and 3 C-F bonds, totaling 4; the ether bridge connecting the upper and lower two aromatic rings has 2 C-O bonds; the lower benzene ring has 6 intra-ring bonds; the lower side chain has 1 aryl-C bond, 1 C=C bond counted as one bond, 2 C-O bonds connected to methoxy oxygens, and 2 O-CH3 bonds, totaling 6. The total is 6 + 4 + 2 + 6 + 6 = 24.

method.method_draft: Assign heavy-atom degrees from the drawing. Top pyridine ring: two substituted ring atoms have degree 3 and four ring atoms have degree 2, giving 14. CF3 group: central carbon degree 4 and three F atoms degree 1 each, giving 7. Bridging O has degree 2. Lower benzene ring: two substituted ring carbons degree 3 and four other ring carbons degree 2, giving 14. Lower alkene/acetal side chain outside the ring: first alkene carbon degree 2, second alkene carbon degree 3, two methoxy oxygens degree 2 each, and two methyl carbons degree 1 each, giving 11. Total degree sum = 14 + 7 + 2 + 14 + 11 = 48; divide by 2 to get 24 bonds.
